severity.description: Business impact of the event. Fixed at level 5 across all event types.

corridorKey.description: Origin country, origin airport and destination airport as ONE token. Origin and destination are never generated independently, so an unroutable pair cannot occur. The five values are exactly the routes exercised by the workshop's own test prompts. Subscribe with `SG-*` for Singapore departures, `SG-SIN-HND` for one route.

disruptionType.description: Replaces the former {flightKey} level. Far more useful to subscribe on — an agent that only cares about cancellations can say so in the subscription rather than in a prompt.

occurredAt.description: When the operational change was recorded. Generate as recent past.

corridor.description: Identical enum to the {corridorKey} topic parameter. In `stm feed configure`, MAP the {corridorKey} topic parameter to this payload field so the two are guaranteed identical. If your STM version does not support topic parameter mapping, delete this field and have TripGuardianAgent read the corridor from the topic string instead — the topic is authoritative.

flightNumber.description: COSMETIC ONLY — makes the event read like a real ops feed. Generated from a pattern, so it will NOT exist in flight_offers.flight_no. Never look it up. FlightSearchAgent finds alternatives by querying the corridor's route.

scheduledDepartureUtc.description: Originally scheduled departure. Generate as near future (0-14 days).

type.description: Identical enum to the {disruptionType} topic parameter, same casing, so the two can be bound by topic parameter mapping.

delayMinutes.description: Minutes of delay. Zero for CANCELLATION and GATE_CHANGE. Deliberately no newDepartureUtc field — the agent derives it from scheduledDepartureUtc + delayMinutes, so the two can never contradict each other.

bookingRef.description: PNR of an affected booking. Correlates to a watched trip.

info.title: Trip Disruption Ops Hub
info.description:
Operational event stream that disrupts trips already planned by the
Solace Agent Mesh Multi-Agent Travel Planning workshop.

Publishes four classes of real-world event (flight irregularities, weather
alerts, hotel property impacts, ground advisories) and consumes the decision
event that Solace Agent Mesh emits after it repairs an itinerary.

DESIGN CONSTRAINTS FOR STM FEED GENERATION
------------------------------------------
1. Every topic parameter and payload field is generated INDEPENDENTLY by
   Faker. Correlated values (country+city, airline+flight number) are
   therefore folded into a single composite level rather than split across
   two levels, so they can never drift apart.
2. Events carry IDENTIFIERS plus WHAT CHANGED. They deliberately do NOT
   carry reference data (airline name, city name, aircraft type, star
   rating, room descriptions). The SAM agents enrich from the `amadeus`
   PostgreSQL database, which is the system of record. This removes almost
   all cross-field consistency risk.
3. No event carries both a start timestamp and an end timestamp. End times
   are expressed as durations, which are always internally consistent.
4. All free text is drawn from curated enums, never from Faker lorem.

TOPIC SHAPE
-----------
  travel/<object>/<verb>/<version>/<severity>/<where>/<specifics...>

`severity` is always level 5 and `where` is always level 6 across every
event type, so cross-domain subscriptions work without payload knowledge:

  travel/>                            all events
  travel/*/*/v1/critical/>            all critical events, any domain
  travel/*/*/v1/*/JP-*/>              everything happening in Japan
  travel/flight/status-changed/v1/*/*/*/SQ*/>   one airline's disruptions
